title: Differential Gene Expression of BRCA1, ERBB2 and TP53 Biomarkers between Human Breast Tissue and Peripheral Blood Samples of Breast Cancer Patients
biological_material: breast tumor tissue and peripheral blood
classification_reason: The comparison group is peripheral blood rather than paired normal breast tissue.
limitations: Does not directly test tumor tissue versus paired normal breast tissue.

title: Gene expression patterns distinguish breast carcinomas from normal breast tissues: the Malaysian context
authors: Ivyna Bong Pau Ni; Zubaidah Zakaria; Rohaizak Muhammad; Norlia Abdullah; Naqiyah Ibrahim; Nor Aina Emran; Nor Hisham Abdullah; Sharifah Noor Akmal Syed Hussain
biological_material: primary breast carcinoma and patient-matched normal breast tissue
main_finding: CD24 was significantly overexpressed in breast carcinoma tissue relative to matched normal tissue.
evidence_passage: CD24 was reported as overexpressed in the tumor group.
classification_reason: The study directly compared paired tumor and normal breast tissues and reported higher CD24 expression in tumors.
limitations: No microdissection; the authors noted possible mixing of tumor and normal cells. The reported differentially expressed genes were not individually validated by qRT-PCR.

title: CD24 expression is a new prognostic marker in breast cancer
main_finding: CD24 protein expression was observed in 84.6% of invasive breast carcinomas and was associated with patient outcomes.
evidence_passage: CD24 expression was observed in 84.6% of invasive breast carcinomas.
classification_reason: The study demonstrates frequent CD24 protein expression in breast tumors but does not directly compare CD24 transcript levels in paired tumor and normal breast tissue.
limitations: Protein staining cannot be treated as identical to mRNA expression; no matched normal comparison addresses the precise claim.

title: Amplification of the CD24 Gene Is an Independent Predictor for Poor Prognosis of Breast Cancer
authors: Peng Zhang; Pan Zheng; Yang Liu
main_finding: CD24 amplification strongly correlated with CD24 mRNA overexpression and was associated with poor survival.
evidence_passage: CD24 amplification strongly correlated with its mRNA overexpression.
classification_reason: The study supports CD24 mRNA overexpression within breast cancer but does not directly compare paired tumor and normal breast tissues.
limitations: The main analysis concerns copy-number status and prognosis rather than the precise tumor-versus-normal claim.

title: Prospective identification of tumorigenic breast cancer cells
authors: Michael Al-Hajj; Max S Wicha; Adalberto Benito-Hernandez; Sean J Morrison; Michael F Clarke
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
main_finding: A CD44-positive and CD24-negative-or-low breast cancer cell population showed strong tumor-forming ability.
evidence_passage: Tumorigenic breast cancer cells were enriched in a CD44-positive and CD24-negative-or-low population.
classification_reason: The study concerns CD24 levels in a tumorigenic cell subpopulation rather than average transcript expression in whole tumor versus paired normal tissue.
limitations: Different biological question and measurement method; it should not be misread as direct contradiction of tissue-level expression.
